defects.title: REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES does not reach the nt_ twin, so the by-name channel clears only half of an ND kernel
defects.failure_scenario: build_registry() registers every mode=="nd" kernel twice -- once as `name` (ND face) and once as `nt_<name>` (NT face) -- and both _make_spec calls receive the SAME base meta dict. So the decorator route (@op(..., real_valued=True)) clears both twins, but the override route is `name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES`, which only ever matches one of the two spellings. Measured on this tree (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/attack2.py, sections C and D): with `catalog.REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES.add("ts_outlier_33")`, `build_registry().get("ts_outlier_33").non_root` is False (cleared) while `build_registry().get("nt_ts_outlier_33").non_root` is still True; same for a throwaway nd kernel (base False / nt_ True). A WP11 plugin that declares an ND kernel it does not own therefore re-admits it to searchable(include_boolean=False) on the ND face only, and silently not on the NT face -- the opposite of the design's "one declaration fixes both levers". It does not bite the declaration the design actually plans (in_sustain_mean/_stddev/_product are dt-face and have no nt_ twin, which is why nothing breaks today), so this is a trap for later packages, not a current wrong result.
defects.suggested_fix: In _make_spec, let an override on the base name cover the derived twin: `real = bool(meta.get("real_valued", False)) or name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES or (face == "nt" and name.startswith("nt_") and name[3:] in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES)`. Add a test registering a throwaway `@op("nd", "cs", arity=1)` boolean kernel, putting only the base name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES, and asserting both `get(n).non_root` and `get("nt_"+n).non_root` are False. If the current behaviour is deliberate instead, say so in the comment at catalog.py:395-400 so WP11 knows it must list both spellings.

defects.title: A name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES that matches no registered operator is a silent no-op
defects.failure_scenario: REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES is only ever consulted as `name in REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES` inside _make_spec; nothing checks afterwards that every name in the set was actually seen. Measured: `catalog.REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES.add("in_sustian_mean")` (one transposed letter) builds cleanly and leaves searchable(include_boolean=False) at 218 with no warning. The failure mode for WP11 is that the plugin believes it moved the GP vocabulary 214 -> 217 while it is still 214, and the only visible symptom is a search trajectory that differs from the intended one -- there is no error, no log line, and no test that would catch it on the plugin side either (the kernel simply stays non_root). The same silence hides a name that was legal but got excluded by EXCLUDED_KERNELS or skipped by _validate.
defects.suggested_fix: At the end of build_registry, before `return reg`, add `unknown = set(REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES) - set(reg._ops)` and either `warnings.warn(f"REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES names no operator: {sorted(unknown)}")` or raise ValueError (raising is safe today because the set is empty by default, so no existing run can hit it). Pin it with a test that adds a typo'd name and asserts the warning/raise.

defects.title: No test distinguishes "skips the probes" from "runs the probes and overwrites the result"
defects.failure_scenario: The design's §5 wording is explicit that _make_spec must SKIP the probes rather than override their result, and the implementation does (counted: a plain build calls _probe_distinct_values 244 times and _probe_constant_capable 29 times; with the three in_sustain stats declared it is 241 / 26). But nothing pins it. Mutation M7 -- rewrite _make_spec to run the try/except + trivial expression first and then do `if real: distinct, trivial = 10 ** 9, False` -- leaves tests/test_real_valued_flag.py and tests/test_catalog.py fully green (16 passed), i.e. the two synthetic-kernel tests pass identically whether the kernel was probed or not. That is the whole point of the declaration for a plugin whose kernel is slow, hangs, or crashes the probe, and it is exactly the regression a future refactor of _make_spec would introduce unnoticed. (13 of the 14 mutants I injected were caught; this is the only survivor. Harness: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/mutate.py.)
defects.suggested_fix: Add a test whose fake kernel records that it was called -- e.g. `calls = []` and `def fn(x): calls.append(1); return (x > 0).float()` -- register it with real_valued=True, call build_registry(), and assert `calls == []` beyond the _validate smoke call (or, more simply, make the kernel raise on the (40, 9) float input the probes use and assert build_registry() still returns a spec with boolean_output False). A monkeypatched counter around catalog._probe_distinct_values / _probe_constant_capable works too and is what I used.

defects.title: catalog.DAILY_FIELDS and WP2's dailyfields.py field tuples will be two unsynchronised copies of the same 9 names
defects.failure_scenario: WP1 puts STORED_DAILY_FIELDS / DERIVED_DAILY_FIELDS / LOG_DAILY_FIELDS in catalog.py (correct per the design), while WP2 adds a separate STORED_FIELDS / DERIVED_FIELDS / LOG_OF in the new dailyfields.py, which the design forbids from importing catalog.py. The two are joined only by the literal spellings. If they drift -- say dailyfields.py spells it "ListAge" but catalog.py keeps "ListAge" and someone later renames one -- the name still PARSES (parser.name() consults reg.daily_fields, fed from catalog.DAILY_FIELDS) but dailyfields.resolve() has no entry for it, so the failure surfaces at engine time on a production run as a KeyError/ValueError inside a leaf reader, not at import or parse time. Nothing in WP1 or in the design's WP2 test list cross-checks the two sets. I verified the 9 spellings in catalog.py match the design's "The field set" section exactly, so there is no drift today.
defects.suggested_fix: In WP2's tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py add a two-line guard: `from alphacube import catalog, dailyfields; assert catalog.STORED_DAILY_FIELDS == dailyfields.STORED_FIELDS and catalog.DERIVED_DAILY_FIELDS == dailyfields.DERIVED_FIELDS and catalog.LOG_DAILY_FIELDS == tuple(dailyfields.LOG_OF) and set(catalog.DAILY_FIELDS) == set(dailyfields.available(None)) | set(dailyfields.STORED_FIELDS)` (adjust the last clause to whatever available(None) returns). A test file may import both modules even though the modules themselves may not import each other.

VERDICT: approved. No high or medium defect. The commit implements all 8 design steps and all 6 listed tests faithfully, touches exactly the 4 files WP1 owns, and I could not make the default path diverge from the baseline in any way I tested.

SCOPE / HYGIENE
- `git diff --name-only 517fd09 1167f00` = src/alphacube/catalog.py, src/alphacube/operators/common.py, tests/test_catalog.py, tests/test_real_valued_flag.py. Nothing outside the owned list. Working tree of /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering is clean; /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube stays at 517fd09 with an empty `git status --porcelain`; my scratch work is confined to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/ (gitignored, nothing committed).
- `real_valued=True` appears nowhere in src/ -- design step 8 ("apply the flag to nothing") is honoured.

(b) DEFAULT-PATH / RANDOM-STREAM IDENTITY -- the strongest evidence, and it is clean
I dumped a canonical snapshot from BOTH trees in separate processes (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP1/run2/dump.py, baseline via PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src) and diffed every key:
- 244 specs x 17 attributes each (name/face/family/category/arity/requires_window/kernel_id/compute_axis/reduces_m/restores_m/lookahead/boolean_output/coarse_output/trivial_boolean/resource_risk/windows/non_root) -- IDENTICAL. Also the 50-entry `skipped` list, `fields`, `constants`.
- searchable() 240 / searchable(include_boolean=False) 218 / (+include_resource_risk=False) 214 -- unchanged.
- TypedTreeGenerator(reg, seed=7): 400 generated trees byte-identical, and the five `_rng.random()` draws taken afterwards identical (so no extra RNG consumption). gen.fields and gen.specs (214 names) identical.
- A second generator (seed=11): 240 mutate_subtree / mutate_window / mutate_constant / crossover results identical, plus the trailing rng draws.
- Vocabulary(reg): fields, windows and the 214 operator names identical.
Mechanically this is expected: the only non-default branch is `if real:`, and `real` is False for every kernel (REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES is empty, no call site passes the keyword); the else branch is the old code verbatim with the same short-circuit (`distinct <= 2 and _probe_constant_capable(...)`) and the same relative ordering against _probe_per_element_python. All three probes use their own torch.Generator().manual_seed(7/11/5) -- no shared or global RNG -- so skipping one cannot perturb another.

(c) NEW CODE PATH, EXERCISED
- Probes are genuinely skipped, counted by monkeypatching: plain build = 244 distinct-probe calls / 29 constant-probe calls; with the three in_sustain stats declared = 241 / 26.
- The comment's measurement is exact: declaring in_sustain_mean+_stddev+_product gives 221/217, and the per-kernel decrements are 219/215 -> 220/216 -> 221/217. `in_sustain` itself stays boolean_output and trivial_boolean when not declared.
- `real=True` sets distinct=10**9, so boolean_output False, coarse_output False (10**9 is above both the <=2 and the 2<x<=3 bands), trivial_boolean False -> non_root False -> re-admitted to searchable(include_boolean=False). Verified directly.
- `meta.get`, not `meta[...]`: confirmed necessary -- mutant M14 (`meta["real_valued"]`) blows up build_registry on the three manual binaries (pow/greater/less) and takes 6 failures + 7 errors with it.
- Baked variants inherit the base kernel's real_valued through `{**base, ...}` (ts_outlier real_valued=True -> ts_outlier_33 and nt_ts_outlier_33 both cleared). Reasonable, and the design is silent on it.
- Registry.fields and Registry.daily_fields are disjoint and parallel; none of the 9 daily names is a registered operator; default_full_catalog() specs are untouched by real_valued (they carry all three flags False already, so no new asymmetry).
- No caller is broken: `Registry(` has exactly one production construction site (catalog.py:448); no `@op(...)` call site in src/ passes more than `pair` positionally, so the new trailing keyword cannot be swallowed; nothing else reads the meta dict by anything but named keys (operators/__init__.py, fullcatalog.py:116), and no test asserts the meta dict's key set.

(d) TEST QUALITY -- mutation-tested, 13/14 caught
I copied the tree to a throwaway dir and injected 14 mutants (run2/mutate.py), running only tests/test_real_valued_flag.py + tests/test_catalog.py each time. Caught: op() dropping the key from meta; _make_spec ignoring the decorator flag; ignoring REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES; forgetting to clear trivial; pinning distinct into the coarse band (3) or the boolean band (2); Registry dropping the argument; build_registry not forwarding it; build_registry defaulting it to (); leaking daily names into `fields`; a one-letter typo in a daily field name; a daily name colliding with "Amt"; meta[...] instead of meta.get. Only survivor is defect 3 above. The pinned 29/22/0 sets and 218/214 counts in the new file are the first thing in the suite to pin them, which is the mis-flag tripwire the design asked for.
Test-pollution check: the fake-kernel fixture writes into the global OPERATOR_REGISTRY, so I forced the adversarial order (`pytest tests/test_real_valued_flag.py::test_real_valued_flag_skips_the_probes ::test_boolean_and_trivial_sets_pinned ::test_searchable_counts_pinned ...`) to make the fake kernel exist before the session-scoped `registry`/default_registry() singleton is first built -- still green, so the try/finally teardown closes that hole.

OBSERVATIONS THAT ARE NOT DEFECTS, FOR THE RECORD
1. The asymmetric default is deliberate and matches the design verbatim: `Registry(fields)` -> daily_fields == (), but `build_registry()`/`default_registry()` -> the 9 names. Both are now pinned by tests. WP2's parser branch reads reg.daily_fields off default_registry(), so it will see the 9 names.
2. `default_registry()` caches _DEFAULT, so a plugin that mutates REAL_VALUED_OVERRIDES after the first default_registry() call has no effect (verified: late `add("eq")` leaves the cached spec non_root True while a fresh build_registry() gives False). The design puts the _DEFAULT reset in WP7's load_plugins, so this is WP7's responsibility, not a WP1 gap -- but WP7 must actually do it.
3. Cost: build_registry() is ~0.2-1.0 s depending on warm-up, and the new tests add ~12 build_registry() calls. Measured incremental cost of the two new test files together is ~3 s; the full suite ran 160 s here vs the design's documented 125.6 s baseline, which I attribute mostly to machine variance (I did not time the baseline tree, because running pytest there would write .pytest_cache/__pycache__ into the read-only baseline worktree).
4. Cosmetic: build_registry's continuation line at catalog.py:447 is indented one space past the open paren (E128); there is no flake8/ruff config or lint test in the repo, so nothing enforces it.
5. COMMIT ATTRIBUTION -- for the orchestrator, not a code issue. The task text required the final line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; commit 1167f00 ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. The implementer flagged this and explained the reasoning (its own harness reminder named Sonnet 5, and the computed task text was marked as carrying no user authority). defects.title: register_scorer makes plugin loading non-idempotent: the design's own load_plugins (WP7) + register() (WP11) crash on a second load
defects.failure_scenario: The duplicate guard fires even when the SAME factory object is re-registered, and nothing downstream makes registration run only once. Reproduced in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP6/sim_wp7.py, which implements WP7 step 1's load_plugins verbatim (importlib.import_module each, call register() if callable) over a module whose register() is the design's WP11 snippet verbatim (`register_scorer('partura', _partura_scorer_factory)`): the first load succeeds, the second dies with `ValueError: scorer kind 'partura' is already registered (pass replace=True to override it)`. import_module is cached, so the module body does not re-run, but load_plugins calls register() again regardless. Three flows hit this as designed: (1) WP8 step 11 builds the plugin list from `--plugin` args PLUS ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS and the design never says it dedups, so `ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS=partura.ac_plugin` together with `--plugin partura.ac_plugin` kills the run before any mining (`load_plugins(['fakeplugin','fakeplugin'])` in the same script raises identically); (2) WP8's own tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py lists at least two cli.main([... '--plugin', '<tmp module>' ...]) cases in one pytest process, so the second one fails; (3) Partura's idea_search.py loops arms and would crash if load_plugins is ever moved inside the loop.
defects.suggested_fix: Make an identical re-registration a no-op, in scoring.py line 536: `if kind in SCORER_FACTORIES and SCORER_FACTORIES[kind] is not factory and not replace: raise ValueError(...)`. A genuine collision (a DIFFERENT factory under the same name) still raises, which is what the design's rule is for. Pin it with a test (`register_scorer('k', F); register_scorer('k', F)` must not raise; `register_scorer('k', G)` must). The alternative — WP7's load_plugins dedups names AND WP11's register() passes replace=True — needs two later packages to both remember, and replace=True there would also silently mask a real name clash between two plugins.

defects.title: make_scorer treats a factory registered as None as "not registered" and blames AlphaCube for a plugin's error
defects.failure_scenario: register_scorer never checks that `factory` is callable, and make_scorer's membership test is `SCORER_FACTORIES.get(kind) is not None` rather than `kind in SCORER_FACTORIES`. result.notes:
DEFECT 1 -- "register_scorer makes plugin loading non-idempotent" -- CONFIRMED AND FIXED.

Reproduced before touching anything, by running the reviewer's own /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP6/sim_wp7.py (WP7 step 1's load_plugins and WP11 step 3's register(), both verbatim) against the unfixed source: the first load_plugins(['fakeplugin']) succeeded, the second died with `ValueError: scorer kind 'partura' is already registered (pass replace=True to override it)`, and load_plugins(['fakeplugin','fakeplugin']) in one call raised identically. The mechanism is exactly as described: importlib.import_module is cached so the module body does not re-run and the factory object is the same object, but load_plugins calls register() again regardless, and the guard did not look at the factory at all.

Fix, scoring.py line 536 (now 540), the reviewer's suggested shape:
  if kind in SCORER_FACTORIES and SCORER_FACTORIES[kind] is not factory and not replace:
The FITNESS_KINDS check above it is untouched and still unconditional, so a built-in name is still refused even with replace=True.

Verified both directions through the same loader shape, not only at the API:
- same module loaded twice, and named twice in one load_plugins call -> both now silent (re-ran sim_wp7.py post-fix);
- two DIFFERENT plugin modules both calling register_scorer('partura', ...) -> still raises (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/fix_WP6/clash.py). The guard still does the job it exists for.

I took identity (`is not`) rather than `==`: the design's WP11 factory is a module-level function, for which `==` is identity anyway, and `is` cannot be perturbed by a factory object defining a strange `__eq__`. A plugin that builds a fresh closure or functools.partial on every register() call would still collide with itself; that is a plugin bug and now has a clear message pointing at it.

I did NOT take the alternative the reviewer also listed (WP7's load_plugins dedups names plus WP11's register() passing replace=True), for the reason given: it needs two later packages to both remember, and replace=True inside a plugin would silently mask a genuine clash between two plugins.

Regression tests, both in tests/test_scorer_registry.py:
- test_registering_the_same_factory_again_is_a_no_op: the same factory twice (and once more with replace=True) must not raise, SCORER_FACTORIES still maps to it, scorer_kinds() lists it once, make_scorer still builds it; then a different factory under that name still raises and does not displace the installed one.
- test_a_plugins_register_hook_survives_being_called_twice: a plugin-shaped register() closing over one factory, called three times in one process -- the loader's actual shape.

THREE SUB-CLAIMS IN THE DEFECT'S "three flows hit this as designed" THAT ARE WEAKER THAN WRITTEN (the defect itself stands; these only matter if the coordinator reuses the reviewer's wording):
(1) "ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS=partura.ac_plugin together with --plugin partura.ac_plugin" -- this reads WP8 step 11's prose ("collect plugin names from args plus ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS"). The design's own main() snippet under "`--plugin` and the CLI" is `list(args.plugin) or [x for x in os.environ...]`, an `or`, so under the snippet --plugin SUPPRESSES the env var and that exact pair never duplicates. The design is internally inconsistent here and WP8 should settle it. The duplicate is reachable either way, because --plugin is repeatable (WP8 step 10), so `--plugin X --plugin X` alone produces it -- that is the load_plugins(['p','p']) case I reproduced.
(2) "WP8's own tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py lists at least two cli.main([... '--plugin' ...]) cases" -- by my reading of WP8's test list, exactly one listed case clearly passes --plugin (the mine case); the others are --fitness nonsense, research/calculate with --daily-fields only, and an explicit no-plugin case. The count is overstated, though any second --plugin test WP8's implementer adds would have hit it.
(3) "Partura's idea_search.py ... would crash if load_plugins is ever moved inside the loop" -- correctly stated as conditional; WP11 step 6 puts the single load_plugins at start-up, outside the arm loop.

NOT TOUCHED (checked, found correct, left alone): the built-in-name guard and its unconditional precedence over replace; make_scorer's three-branch order and the unchanged PanelScorer fall-through; scorer_kinds()'s ordering; __all__; the dates/warmup forwarding. All three defects reproduced before any edit, and all three are real. Per defect:

Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a9_listage_view_anchored.py (10 symbols x 60 days, unlisted_days=8, so the last symbol lists on store day 8).

  st.view().daily("ListAge")                        -> store day 30: young symbol 22.0, old symbol 10030.0  (2 distinct values in the cross-section)
  st.view(start=dates[20]).daily("ListAge")         -> the SAME store day 30: young symbol 10010.0, old symbol 10010.0  (1 distinct value)
  warmed_view(st, start=dates[30], end=dates[50], warmup=10).daily("ListAge") -> store day 30 column is [10010.]*10  (1 distinct value)

Two consequences, both silent:

(2) Every symbol listed before the window's first day gets LIST_AGE_SENTINEL + d, so on a windowed view the plane is constant across the cross-section: cs_rank(ListAge) / cs_zscore(ListAge) are a flat tie / all-zero, i.e. any ListAge factor silently carries zero information. defects.suggested_fix:
Anchor the lifecycle counter to the store, then slice to the window, inside CubeView.daily() — the one place that knows both axes. E.g. special-case the lifecycle-dependent field before the generic resolve call at store.py:539-541:

    if name == "ListAge":
        rows = self._rows(0, self.n_symbols)
        full_status = self.store.read_status(rows, 0, self.store.n_days)
        plane = resolve(name, self.symbols, self.store.dates, store=self.store.daily, status=full_status)
        self._daily[name] = np.ascontiguousarray(plane[:, self.d0:self.d1])
    else:
        self._daily[name] = resolve(name, self.symbols, self.dates, ...)

(Equivalently: give dailyfields.derive a `day_offset`/`first_date_index` argument so the sticky cumsum starts at the store's day 0.) That costs one extra (S_view x D_store) int8 read per view, is identical on a full view (so tests/test_daily_fields_store.py:382 stays green), and makes ListAge satisfy the same view-independence property as FloatCap/LimitWidth/BoardCode. Then extend the ListAge test to assert exactly that: `st.view(start=dates[20]).daily("ListAge") == st.view().daily("ListAge")[:, 20:]`.

defects.title: daily() passes the raw status plane to a helper that hardcodes OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE == 0, bypassing the store's own day_status_codes map
defects.failure_scenario: CubeStore builds `self._codes = {**DAY_STATUS_CODES, **self.meta.get("day_status_codes", {})}` so a store may legitimately remap the codes, and every other reader honours that map (CubeStore.tradable():189, SegmentedCubeStore.read_status():420 fills with `self._codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"]`, CubeView.tradable():486 reads `getattr(self.store, "_codes", ...)`). CubeView.daily() hands `status=self.day_status()` straight to dailyfields._lifecycle_mask, which tests `status != _OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE` with `_OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE = 0` hardcoded (dailyfields.py:86). On a store whose meta declares e.g. `{"OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE": 9}`, every not-yet-listed stock-day is read as in-lifecycle, so ListAge silently reports the sentinel for a stock that had not listed yet — no error, no warning. No store in the tree remaps the codes today, which is why the suite is green; the meta key exists precisely to allow it.
defects.suggested_fix: Translate at the boundary, where the code map is in hand. In CubeView.daily(), pass a lifecycle boolean instead of a raw code plane: `codes = getattr(self.store, "_codes", DAY_STATUS_CODES)` then `status=None, tradable=(self.day_status() != codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"])` — _lifecycle_mask's `tradable` branch already means exactly "True counts toward ListAge". (Alternatively give dailyfields.resolve an `outside_lifecycle=0` keyword and pass `codes["OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE"]`.) Add a test that builds a store via build_cube_store(..., extra_meta={"day_status_codes": {...remapped...}}) and checks ListAge still NaNs the unlisted prefix.

defects.title: daily_s/daily_d hand out writable views into the per-view cache, unlike read_s/read_d which copy
defects.failure_scenario: `return self.daily(name)[s_lo:s_hi, :]` is a basic numpy slice, so it aliases the cached plane and is writable. Measured (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP3/a3_misc_edges.py): `np.shares_memory(view.daily_s("FloatCap", 0, 3), view.daily("FloatCap")) is True`, `writeable is True`, and writing to the slice leaves the cached plane permanently corrupted (`view.daily("FloatCap")[0, :3] -> [-1. -1. -1.]`) for every later chunk and every later consuming edge in the same view. read_s/read_d return a fresh `np.array(..., copy=True)` per call, so the engine has never had to care. WP4 is told to use daily_s/daily_d "exactly as read_s/read_d are used today" and will wrap them in `torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(sl))`; for MODE_S the ascontiguousarray is a no-op and `.to(cpu, float32)` returns the same tensor, so the tensor aliases the cache. Nothing mutates a leaf in place today (I grepped src/alphacube/operators for in-place torch ops and every hit writes to a freshly allocated output), so this is latent rather than live — but it is a silent-wrong-numbers failure mode if it ever stops being true, and it costs one line to close.
defects.suggested_fix: Freeze the cache once, in daily(): `arr = resolve(...); arr.setflags(write=False); self._daily[name] = arr`. An accidental in-place write then raises ValueError instead of corrupting the plane, and WP4's `np.ascontiguousarray` + `torch.from_numpy` still works (it only emits torch's non-writable-array UserWarning, which this suite already carries elsewhere). If you would rather avoid that warning, have daily_s/daily_d return `np.array(self.daily(name)[...], copy=True)` and drop the "thin slice" wording from the docstrings.

JUDGMENT CALL on op_weight's accepted shape, since the design text is internally ambiguous here (not a source-vs-design conflict, since this is new code): the '2. Generator' code stub types op_weight strictly as Callable[[OpSpec], float], but the WP5 construction-time-validation prose says 'every op_weight key names a registered operator; every value is a finite float >= 0' and the test list says 'an unknown operator name ... each raise at __init__' and 'a weight table that empties the pool' -- vocabulary (key/value/table) that only makes sense for a Mapping, and a pure callable gives __init__ no way to ever see an 'unknown name' (it is only ever called with real OpSpec objects already pulled from the registry). Resolution shipped: op_weight accepts EITHER a callable(OpSpec)->float (called directly, exactly as the design's pseudocode shows) OR a {operator name: weight} Mapping (validated against the registry and wrapped into such a callable by the new _resolve_op_weight; an unlisted name defaults to the uniform weight 1.0). self.op_weight is always, after __init__, the callable form -- so _pick_weighted's code is unaffected and matches the design's pseudocode verbatim. Flagging this because WP7's SearchHooks (not yet built) forwards its own op_weight straight into this parameter: either shape works.

Found and had to work around a real tension inside the design's own WP5 text, not a mistake on my part: a literally-all-zero op_weight (e.g. `lambda s: 0.0`) is simultaneously (a) the worked example for 'all-zero weights still return an operator via the uniform fallback' in the generator test-plan bullet, and (b) exactly what 'a weight table that empties the 26-spec reduce pool' means in the construction-time-validation bullet -- and (b) is required to raise ValueError at __init__. These cannot both be true of the SAME op_weight value. Resolution: construction-time validation raises for a GLOBALLY all-zero (or pool-emptying) op_weight, as the design's own IndexError/ShapeError-forever justification demands. The 'all-zero weights still return an operator' property is real and tested, but as a property of `_pick_weighted` itself for an arbitrary draw whose specs happen to be all zero-weighted (e.g. a single mutate_operator call's narrow per-node `alts`, which __init__ cannot enumerate ahead of time) -- tested in test_op_weight_all_zero_for_one_draw_still_returns_an_operator and test_op_weight_uniformly_zero_draw_matches_the_plain_uniform_path by reassigning gen.op_weight AFTER construction (bypassing the one-time __init__ check) and calling _pick/_pick_weighted directly.
result.notes:
New public names on TypedTreeGenerator, for WP7's SearchHooks and Partura's ac_plugin to build on: constructor keywords op_weight, accept, daily_fields, daily_leaf_prob, leaf_slots, on_exhausted ('fallback'|'raise'), mutation_checks_bans (bool); new attributes self.op_weight (always a callable(OpSpec)->float after __init__, or None), self.accept_hook, self.hook_rng (a second random.Random, seeded (seed*2654435761)&0xFFFFFFFF -- any accept hook MUST draw from gen.hook_rng, never gen._rng, or the steer/control comparison stops being reproducible from the seed), self.unaccepted_fallbacks (int counter); public method acceptable() unchanged in signature but now also consults the hook; new private _ban_ok/_pick_weighted/_resolve_op_weight/_check_weight/_check_accept_hook helpers (not exported); module now exports GenerationExhausted(ValueError) via __all__, plus the module-level GENERATE_FALLBACK_TRIES=64 constant (importable but not added to __all__, matching the design's instruction to export only GenerationExhausted). acceptable()'s order is is_valid_root -> _ban_ok -> accept_hook, matching the design exactly, including the short-circuit that keeps one_layer_keys() uncomputed when there is no ban set.

Backward compatibility was the thing I verified hardest, two independent ways: (1) an RNG-call-sequence recorder (random.Random subclass logging every method name) run through the new _pick versus a hand-frozen copy of the literal pre-WP5 _pick body, confirming identical call sequences AND identical picks, not just equal keys; (2) [e.key() for e in generate_population(40)] identical between a plain generator and one constructed with every new keyword passed explicitly at its documented default. Both pass. The two "deliberate behaviour changes" the design calls out (mutate_window/mutate_constant now checking the ban+hook; generate()'s fallback now checking them too) are pinned with the design's own two concrete leak examples (cross_quantile_q25(day_argmax(Low), 3) under O:day_argmax(F:Low) banned; mul(day_cov(Volume, Low), 2.0) under O:day_cov(F:Volume,F:Low) banned), each shown to leak under mutation_checks_bans=False and to be sealed under the new default.

Low-confidence spot for a reviewer to double check: the exact wording of the ValueError messages (op_weight emptying the pool; negative/NaN weight; unknown operator name; bad accept) -- the design says only "Raise ValueError naming the cause", not exact strings, so I chose the phrasing myself (visible in generator.py's _check_weight/_check_accept_hook/_resolve_op_weight/__init__). If WP7's tests or Partura's own error-matching code string-match on exact phrasing, they will need to match what I actually shipped. Also: op_weight's construction-time value check evaluates the hook over self.specs (the generator's own vocabulary, ~214 by default) rather than registry.list_all() (244) -- deliberate, since those are exactly the specs _pick/_pick_weighted ever see, but worth knowing if a future caller expects validation against the full registry instead.

Did not touch mining/gp.py, plugins.py, scoring.py, or anything outside the two owned files -- GPMiner's own hooks=/SearchHooks plumbing is WP7's job per the design's dependency graph (WP5 depends only on WP2, which was already committed in this worktree). Verified via git status/git diff --stat that only the two owned files changed, and the full suite was run against this worktree's own src/ (via the repo-root conftest.py's sys.path insert, confirmed by reading it directly), not any globally installed alphacube.

defects.title: test_generate_fallback_relaxed_tree_still_avoids_an_active_ban_set is vacuous — deleting the _ban_ok check it claims to pin leaves all 27 tests green
defects.failure_scenario: The test's own docstring says "`relaxed` must still track only a tree that is ban_ok (not just any minimal collapse), proving the fallback discriminates on the ban set and not merely on is_valid_root". Delete `self._ban_ok(tree) and` from generator.py:248 (leaving `if relaxed is None and is_valid_root(tree)`) and run `pytest tests/test_generator_hooks.py`: 27 passed. Reproduced with /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP5/mutate.py (MUT=M1_relaxed_no_ban) and again standalone in a4_fake_test.py. The reason it cannot fail: it bans exactly ONE of the ~320 minimal keys the fallback can draw (`victim = next(iter(one_layer_keys(probe._collapse_leaf(pool[0]))))`), so P(first fallback draw is the victim) ~ 0.3% — with seed 2 the un-checked version returns `O:day_durbin_watson(F:Ret)`, which satisfies both assertions. The check is genuinely load-bearing: banning 319 of the 320 reachable minimal keys with an always-False hook, the un-checked version returns a BANNED tree in 40/40 seeds while the shipped code leaks 0/40 (28 raise GenerationExhausted, 12 return the one spare). So the central correctness property of the WP5 fix — the design's deliberate behaviour change (b), "a fallback tree carrying a banned key is no longer returned" — has no test at all, and a future refactor of generate() can reintroduce the leak silently.
defects.suggested_fix: Make the ban set cover the draws. Enumerate the reachable minimal keys once (`keys = set(); for s in probe._root_ops_of('reduce'): for _ in range(400): keys |= one_layer_keys(probe._collapse_leaf(s))` — 320 of them), ban `keys - {spare}` for one chosen `spare`, install `accept=lambda t: False`, and over ~20 seeds assert that `generate()` either raises GenerationExhausted or returns a tree whose one_layer_keys are disjoint from the ban set — never a banned one. Keep the existing single-victim case as a cheap smoke test if desired, but it must not be the thing the docstring's claim rests on.

defects.title: _pick_weighted's face mass divides by the face's full operator count, not by the surviving (weight>0) count, so it does not reproduce Partura's pick
defects.failure_scenario: The design states the semantics normatively twice — §"2. Generator": "a face's mass is its operators' mean weight ... which reproduces Partura's current `pick` exactly, so the migration changes no behaviour" and "Weight 0 is how 'drop this operator from the vocabulary without shifting the draws' is expressed"; WP5 step 7: "This reproduces Partura's current pick semantics exactly, so the migration is behaviour-preserving". Partura's actual pick (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:225-238) filters `if w > 0` BEFORE building the face lists, so `sum(w)/len(faces[n])` divides by the number of SURVIVING operators. The shipped `masses = [sum(weights[face]) / len(weights[face]) ...]` divides by the number of ALL operators in the face, so a face's probability is scaled by its surviving fraction. Measured (a3_partura_pick.py, a6_real_weights.py): zeroing the 55 dt/in operators gives P(dt face) = 0.1404 empirically (0.1406 analytic) under the shipped code vs 0.2485 (0.2500 analytic) under Partura's pick and 0.25 under the uniform path — a 1.8x distortion; with only `day_mean` surviving in dt, 0.0031 vs 0.25 — 81x. Partura runs with allow_resource_risk=True (idea_search.py:321) and `base_weight` zeroes the resource_risk ops in BOTH arms, and the steer arm's `operator_weights()` (partura/steer.py:395) assigns 0.0 for every generic `ban` rule, so the shift is proportional to how many operators a steer config bans per face — and the `shared` face has only 17 members. Consequence: WP11's migration silently changes both arms' operator distribution instead of preserving it, and weight 0 does shift the draws. No test catches it: replacing the mean with a plain sum (MUT=M4_face_mass_sum) leaves all 27 tests green, i.e. nothing pins face-balancing in the weighted path at all.
defects.suggested_fix:
Drop the zero-weight specs from the face before taking the mean, exactly as Partura does, keeping the same two `choices` draws:
```python
live_specs = {f: [(s, w) for s, w in zip(faces[f], weights[f]) if w > 0.0] for f in faces}
live = [f for f in sorted(faces) if live_specs[f]]
if not live:
    return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])
masses = [sum(w for _, w in live_specs[f]) / len(live_specs[f]) for f in live]
face = self._rng.choices(live, weights=masses)[0]
return self._rng.choices([s for s, _ in live_specs[face]], weights=[w for _, w in live_specs[face]])[0]
```
Add the two missing tests: (1) `op_weight=lambda s: 1.0` must give the same face-share distribution as `op_weight=None` over ~100k draws (this is what kills the sum-instead-of-mean mutation); (2) zeroing most of one face must leave that face's share at its uniform value, not at its surviving fraction.

defects.title: hook_rng is random.Random(0) in every mining run, because gp.py constructs the generator with rng= and never seed=
defects.failure_scenario: `self.hook_rng = random.Random((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF)` reads the `seed` keyword, but the only in-tree construction site — gp.py:241, `TypedTreeGenerator(registry, fields=..., n_minutes=..., min_depth=..., max_depth=..., allow_boolean_ops=..., allow_resource_risk=..., rng=self._rng)` — passes `rng=` and no `seed=`, so `seed` stays at its default 0 and the hook stream is `Random(0)` whatever the run's seed. WP7 step 2 says to forward op_weight/accept/daily_fields/daily_leaf_prob/leaf_slots "into the existing TypedTreeGenerator(...) call at line 241" and does not add `seed=`, so the shipped wiring is what WP7 will inherit. Measured (a7_hook_rng.py): GPMiner-style construction with run seeds 0, 7 and 12345 all yield hook_rng first draws [0.844422, 0.757954, 0.420572]; passing `seed=` instead gives three different streams. Two consequences: (a) the whole stated purpose — "an accept hook that needs a uniform draw must use it" so that "the steer/control comparison is reproducible from the seed" — fails in the direction nobody tests: varying the seed does not vary the hook's thinning draws at all, so N seeds of the steer arm share one thinning realisation, and Partura's current hook (idea_search.py:209, seeded from its own SEED) loses seed-dependence when it migrates to gen.hook_rng; (b) with the default seed=0, hook_rng and _rng are the SAME stream (verified: identical first three draws), contradicting the docstring's "a second, independent stream". test_hook_rng_is_a_distinct_deterministic_instance cannot see either problem — it only checks object identity and same-seed determinism.
defects.suggested_fix:
Derive the hook seed from the supplied rng when one is given; `getstate()` does not advance the stream, so this adds no draw and keeps the default path byte-identical:
```python
hook_seed = ((seed * 2654435761) & 0xFFFFFFFF) if rng is None else \
            (hash(rng.getstate()[1]) ^ 0x9E3779B9) & 0xFFFFFFFF
self.hook_rng = random.Random(hook_seed)
```
If WP5 must stay literal to the design text instead, then WP7 has to add `seed=seed` at gp.py:241 and that must be written into WP7's step list, because it is not there today. Either way add a test that two generators built the way gp.py builds them (`rng=random.Random(s)`, no seed=) with s=7 vs s=12345 get different hook_rng streams.

defects.title: on_exhausted is never validated, so a typo silently disables the strict mode
defects.failure_scenario: `self.on_exhausted = on_exhausted` stores the string unchecked and the only reader is `self.on_exhausted == "raise"`. Measured (a2_probes.py): `TypedTreeGenerator(..., accept=lambda t: False, on_exhausted="RAISE")` returns `O:day_quantile_q75(F:Open)` with unaccepted_fallbacks == 1 instead of raising; `on_exhausted="typo"` and `on_exhausted=None` behave the same. The design calls "raise" "the strict variant the correctness judge asked for" — a caller who wants a hard failure when the hook exhausts gets a silent relaxed tree instead, and the counter they would inspect looks like a normal fallback.
defects.suggested_fix: In __init__, next to the other construction-time checks: `if on_exhausted not in ("fallback", "raise"): raise ValueError(f"on_exhausted must be 'fallback' or 'raise', not {on_exhausted!r}")`, and store the validated value. Add it to the construction-rejection test block alongside the op_weight/accept cases.

defects.title: daily_fields and leaf_slots get no construction-time validation, unlike op_weight — misspellings fail late or as IndexError
defects.failure_scenario: op_weight mapping keys are checked against the registry at __init__ ("a typo'd name would otherwise sit silently inert"), but the two new daily-leaf keywords are stored raw. Measured (a2_probes.py, a5_edges.py): `daily_fields=("NotAFieldEither",), daily_leaf_prob=1.0` constructs fine and `_gen("daily", 1, full=False)` returns `DF:NotAFieldEither`, which can only fail later in WP4's leaf reader, i.e. mid-mining-run; `leaf_slots={"nope_xyz": {0: ("NotAField",)}}` is silently inert (the exact failure mode the op_weight check exists to prevent); `leaf_slots={"cs_regres": {7: ("FloatCap",)}}` silently ignores the out-of-range index; and `leaf_slots={"cs_regres": {1: ()}}` raises `IndexError: Cannot choose from an empty sequence` out of `_build` — not a ShapeError, so `_gen`'s `except ShapeError: continue` retry loop does not absorb it and it escapes `generate()`. WP7 step 6 adds exactly this kind of check for DF: ban keys against `registry.daily_fields`, so the registry already carries the information.
defects.suggested_fix: In __init__, after `self.daily_fields = list(daily_fields)`: reject any name not in `registry.daily_fields`. For leaf_slots, reject a key not in `registry` (`name not in registry`), a slot index that is negative or >= the spec's arity, any field name not in `registry.daily_fields`, and an empty field tuple — all ValueError naming the cause, matching the op_weight messages' shape. Extend test_leaf_slots_* with the rejection cases.

defects.title: A weight-0 operator can still be swapped in by mutate_operator via _pick_weighted's uniform fallback
defects.failure_scenario: `mutate_operator` narrows `alts` to one node's (category, arity, face, family) group. When every member of that group is weight 0, `_pick_weighted`'s `live` is empty and the uniform fallback draws from all of them, so a zero-weighted operator enters the child. Measured (a5_edges.py): with the 55 dt/in operators zeroed, 20 of 1200 mutate_operator children carried one, while 0 of 200 freshly generated trees did. The design sanctions the fallback ("a weight function must not be able to make generation impossible") and Partura's own pick has the identical `if not faces: return _pick(self, specs)`, so this is parity rather than a regression — but it means weight 0 is not an exclusion mechanism, and Partura zeroes the resource_risk operators for runtime reasons (idea_search.py:139/217 with allow_resource_risk=True), so a steer arm can still have a resource-risky kernel mutated into its population.
defects.suggested_fix: No code change is required for design conformance; if it should not happen, make the fallback narrow rather than global — when every weight in a given draw is 0, fall back to a uniform draw restricted to the specs that were passed in only if that is the whole vocabulary, and otherwise return None / let mutate_operator's retry loop pick another node. Minimum: state the leak in _pick_weighted's docstring (it currently only says "a weight function must not be able to make generation impossible") so WP11 does not read weight 0 as a vocabulary ban, and add a test pinning the current behaviour either way.

Scratch scripts in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP5/ (a1_stream_identity.py, a2_probes.py, a3_partura_pick.py, a4_fake_test.py, a5_edges.py, a6_real_weights.py, a7_hook_rng.py, mutate.py, old_generator.py); nothing in either worktree was modified.

WHAT I VERIFIED MYSELF RATHER THAN TAKING ON TRUST

(b) Default-path identity, against the TRUE pre-WP5 code, not against another new generator. I extracted generator.py from the parent commit (`git show 6d14711:src/.../generator.py`), loaded it as a sibling module, and compared the real old class to the new one on 12 seeds x 7 parameter combos (defaults, max_depth=5, allow_boolean_ops, allow_resource_risk, include_lookahead, a ban set, max_retries=1/depth 2) using both `[e.key() for e in generate_population(40)]` and a random.Random subclass logging every (method, len) call: 0 mismatches, equal call sequences. Same for all five mutate_* plus crossover over 8 seeds x 12 trees: 0 mismatches. The implementer's claim holds.

Default fallback cannot spuriously raise: `is_valid_root(self._collapse_leaf(s))` is True for every one of the 26 root reducers, 6 field draws each, under all four vocabulary flag combinations — so the `tries == 1` branch always returns on its first candidate and GenerationExhausted is unreachable with no hook and no ban. Spec names are unique (244/244 with include_lookahead), so the name-keyed `weights` dict in __init__ cannot collapse two specs.

(d) Test quality, by mutation testing (mutate.py, 8 mutations, each a verbatim copy of the shipped method with one thing broken). Red as they should be: mutate_window reverted to is_valid_root; mutate_constant reverted; `_pick_weighted` inner draw made uniform; `_build` filling every leaf_slots slot. Survived all 27 tests: (1) `relaxed` without `_ban_ok` -> defect #1; (2) face mass = sum instead of mean -> no test pins face-balancing in the weighted path, folded into defect #2; (3) `acceptable()`'s order swapped so the hook runs before `_ban_ok` — the code is right and matches the design, but nothing pins the order or the "one_layer_keys computed only when a ban set exists" short-circuit; (4) the `self.daily_fields and` guard removed from `_gen` — all 27 new tests pass, BUT the full suite goes red at tests/test_mining.py::test_skip_kernels_reproduces_the_trajectory_until_the_first_refusal (1 failed, 794 passed), which compares two whole GPMiner runs key-for-key. So "the single most important guarantee in the design" is covered — by a pre-existing test, not by this file. Note that test_generate_population_identical_with_all_defaults_made_explicit and test_leaf_slots_and_daily_fields_both_empty_match_the_plain_population compare new-vs-new and therefore cannot detect any default-path regression; they are weak, not wrong, and the design asked for the first one verbatim.

(a) Design conformance, step by step: all 7 keywords with the design's names/defaults/order; all 7 attributes plus hook_rng and unaccepted_fallbacks; the hook_rng doc note; four of the five construction-time rejections exactly as specified (the fifth, "every op_weight key names a registered operator", exists only in the Mapping form — a pure callable has no keys, which is the ambiguity the implementer flagged, and the resolution they shipped is the right reading); `_ban_ok` + acceptable's order; the generate() fallback matching the design's pseudocode and its GenerationExhausted message verbatim; `_pick`'s uniform branch verbatim; the two mutation fixes with the escape hatch; mutate_operator untouched; the daily-leaf branch and the leaf_slots branch exactly as the design's snippets; GenerationExhausted in __all__. The only conformance break is `_pick_weighted`'s denominator (defect #2).

defects.title: open_cube_store's ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS fallback makes the build script crash before it does anything — the script that creates the daily store refuses to run because the daily store does not exist yet
defects.failure_scenario: main() calls open_cube_store(str(store_dir)) with no daily_root, and open_cube_store (src/alphacube/store.py:444-445) does `if daily_root is None: daily_root = os.environ.get("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS")`. That env var is the design's documented way to point AlphaCube at the daily store, so on the server it will most naturally be set to exactly the --out default (/root/autodl-tmp/AlphaCube/daily_fields). On the FIRST build that directory does not exist, so CubeStore.__init__ (store.py:131) does DailyFieldStore(daily_root) and the script dies with an uncaught FileNotFoundError: <out>/meta.json, before the schema probe, the side-by-side symbol print or anything else. Reproduced: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP9/attack_env.py sets os.environ['ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS'] = str(out) and then calls bdf.main([...]) on a synthetic store -> FileNotFoundError at store.py:131 / dailyfields.py:281, traceback, no diagnostics. Same env var also makes the delivered tests environment-dependent: `ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS=/tmp/does_not_exist_daily ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_build_daily_fields.py -q` -> 12 failed, 10 passed (all 14 tests that go through main()). Secondary effect when the env var points at an EXISTING stale store: the script silently attaches it and sha256s its meta.json, which contradicts the design's 'opens the cube store read-only purely for its canonical symbols/dates'.
defects.suggested_fix:
Neutralise the env fallback at the one call site. Either pop/restore it around the open:

    saved = os.environ.pop("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS", None)
    try:
        store = open_cube_store(str(store_dir))
    finally:
        if saved is not None:
            os.environ["ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS"] = saved

or dispatch directly the way open_cube_store does (SegmentedCubeStore(p) when (p/'minute'/META_FILE).is_file() else CubeStore(p)), which also documents 'no daily source is attached while we build one'. Add a regression test with monkeypatch.setenv("ALPHACUBE_DAILY_FIELDS", str(tmp_path / "not_built_yet")) around the happy-path build.

defects.title: A date file whose schema is short of read_cols crashes mid-build with a raw ArrowInvalid that does not name the file
defects.failure_scenario: build_planes does pd.read_parquet(path, columns=read_cols) for every store date, with read_cols fixed from the ONE probed file. In a years-long vendor directory a column can appear or disappear partway through the history. Reproduced (attack_misc.py case A2): a cap-dir where only the first date carries circulating_shares -> the probe sees it, FloatShares is scheduled, and the second date's read raises `pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid: No match for FieldRef.Name(circulating_shares) in symbol: large_string`. The message names neither the date nor the path, the traceback is raw pyarrow, and the whole build (minutes of parquet reads at server scale) is lost. The same happens for a corrupt/truncated parquet or a later file missing total_market_value.
defects.suggested_fix: Wrap the per-date read: `try: df = pd.read_parquet(path, columns=read_cols) except Exception as e: raise SystemExit(f"{path}: cannot read columns {read_cols} ({e}); the schema probed at {sample_path} does not hold for every date") from e`, or (friendlier for an optional field) read the file's schema with pyarrow.parquet.read_schema, skip the columns it lacks, count those dates per field and print the count next to the coverage line so the hole is visible instead of fatal.

defects.title: The published --out directory inherits mkdtemp's 0700 mode, so a reader running as another user cannot open the daily store
defects.failure_scenario: tempfile.mkdtemp always creates the directory with mode 0700, and os.replace carries that mode onto --out. Measured (attack_misc.py case A6): the built daily_fields directory comes out 0o700 while the cube store that write_synthetic_store/build_cube_store produces next to it is 0o755. Any process not running as the building user (a different service account, a mining job under another user, an operator inspecting the files) gets PermissionError on <out>/meta.json, which surfaces downstream as 'daily_root cannot be opened' rather than as a permissions problem.
defects.suggested_fix: Before the rename, give the temp directory the mode a normal mkdir would get: `os.chmod(tmp, 0o777 & ~_umask())` (read the umask with os.umask(0) / os.umask(old)), or simply os.chmod(tmp, 0o755) to match build_cube_store's output. Assert the resulting mode in the primary test.

defects.title: The rebuild refusal fires only after the entire build, instead of as a cheap path check at the start
defects.failure_scenario: The 'out already exists non-empty' refusal lives inside write_daily_field_store, i.e. after the store open, the probe, every parquet read and the coverage gate. Reproduced end-to-end (attack_rerun.py): run1 rc=0, run2 raises SystemExit('could not move the newly built directory into place ... remove it first and re-run'); the old directory is intact and no temp dir leaks, so nothing is damaged, but on the real server the operator pays a full multi-minute build to learn a fact that is knowable from a single stat() call. This is the one place the implementation extends the design's literal step 7, and it is the step an operator hits on every second run (e.g. after adding the real share-column name).
defects.suggested_fix: Add the check to main() right next to refuse_if_out_inside_sources: `if out_dir.exists() and any(out_dir.iterdir()): raise SystemExit(f"{out_dir} already exists and is not empty; remove it first (this script never overwrites a previous build)")` — keeping the late check in write_daily_field_store as the belt-and-braces guard. If rebuilds should instead just work, do the swap atomically: os.replace(tmp, out_dir) when out_dir is absent/empty, else os.replace(out_dir, out_dir.with_name(out_dir.name + ".old")) then os.replace(tmp, out_dir) then rmtree the .old.

defects.title: The test suite does not pin summarize's 'first/last date with any data': always returning the whole date axis stays green
defects.failure_scenario: Mutation (harness /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP9/mutate.py, case M8): replacing summarize's `date_range[name] = (dates[int(has_data[0])], dates[int(has_data[-1])])` with `(dates[0], dates[-1])` leaves tests/test_build_daily_fields.py at 22 passed. A real build whose cap-dir starts later than the store's day axis would report a misleading date_range and nothing would catch it. (8 of the 10 mutations I tried were killed, so this is a gap, not a pattern.)

defects.title: The test suite does not pin the atomic publish: replacing os.replace with shutil.copytree stays green
defects.failure_scenario: Mutation (mutate.py case M10): replacing `os.replace(tmp, out_dir)` with `shutil.copytree(tmp, out_dir)` leaves tests/test_build_daily_fields.py at 22 passed, although it breaks design step 7 outright -- the publish is no longer atomic (a crash during the copy leaves a half-written, DailyFieldStore-openable --out) and every successful run leaves a `.daily_fields.<rand>.tmp` directory behind beside --out forever. test_an_interrupted_write_leaves_nothing_a_daily_field_store_will_open only interrupts inside np.save, i.e. strictly before the rename, so it cannot see this; and no test looks for leftovers after a SUCCESSFUL build.
defects.suggested_fix: Two cheap assertions: (1) in the primary build test, after rc == 0 assert `[p for p in out.parent.glob(f".{out.name}.*")] == []`; (2) add a test that monkeypatches bdf.os.replace to raise OSError and asserts SystemExit, `not out.exists()` and no leftover temp directory -- which pins that the final step is a rename of a fully written directory rather than a per-file copy into --out.

defects.title: test_suspended_stock_day_is_nan_on_every_leaf_reader is vacuous for 2 of the 3 readers: both new tradability masks can be deleted and the whole 860-test suite stays green
defects.failure_scenario:
Mutation-verified twice, against the FULL suite, with the mutant instrumented to prove it fired.

(1) Cube reader. Delete `return self._mask_cube(t, tradable)` from engine.py:246 and return the bare tensor (keeping the shape assertion). Result: `tests/ -q` = 860 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, with the mutant reporting 45 unmasked daily-leaf cube reads actually taken. Yet the behaviour is materially different: on the `daily_view` fixture, `cross_mean(FloatCap, 3)` (a MODE_S round whose only operand IS the daily leaf) changes by max|diff| 1.0e6 over 50 cells.

(2) Panel reader. Make `_run_panel_round.operand`'s branch (engine.py:376-389) return the unmasked (D,S) plane. Result: `tests/ -q` = 860 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, mutant reporting 21 unmasked panel operands taken. Yet `cs_demean(FloatCap)` changes by max|diff| 1.07e9 over 347 cells and `cs_rank(FloatCap)` by max|diff| 0.2 over 262 cells.

Why the two carriers this test names cannot see it: for `_load_leaf_cube` the carrier is `day_mean(mul(Ret, LimitWidth))`, and `Ret` is already NaN on a suspended stock-day, so `Ret * LimitWidth` is NaN whether or not LimitWidth was masked -- the assertion passes either way. For `_run_panel_round` the carrier is `cs_rank(FloatCap)` and the only assertion is `np.array_equal(np.isnan(p), ~trad.T)`; `_run_panel_round` re-masks every node output unconditionally (engine.py:403-408), so the NaN PATTERN is identical with or without the operand mask -- what the operand mask actually protects is the finite values of the TRADABLE stocks on that day, because cs_* is cross-sectional and an unmasked suspended stock joins the cross-section. Only the `parse("FloatCap")` entry (the `_leaf_panel` path) is non-vacuous; I confirmed that one does go red when its mask is removed.

This is the design's own test-plan bullet ("Masking: a suspended stock-day is NaN in the output on both the cube and the panel path"), so the production code is correct but the guard rail the design asked for does not exist -- and WP8/WP10/WP11 all touch the engine next.
defects.suggested_fix:
Add carriers whose VALUE depends on the leaf's masked value and is not NaN-shadowed by a sibling, and assert values rather than only the NaN pattern.

For `_load_leaf_cube`: `cross_mean(FloatCap, 3)` compared against a hand-written numpy reference built from `np.where(view.tradable(), cap, np.nan)` (a day-axis rolling mean over the masked plane). It is a MODE_S round with the daily leaf as its sole operand, so nothing else can supply the NaN.

For `_run_panel_round.operand`: `cs_demean(FloatCap)` against `cap_masked - nanmean(cap_masked, axis=cross-section)`, i.e. assert the finite values, not just `np.isnan`.

Equivalently (or in addition) add two explicit negative tests that monkeypatch each branch to skip masking and assert `not np.array_equal(...)` -- that makes the claim self-checking rather than relying on a carrier staying well chosen.

defects.title: _leaf_panel is called outside evaluate()'s per-root error handling, so one unresolvable bare DailyFeature root loses the whole tolerant=True batch
defects.failure_scenario:
`evaluate()`'s root loop does `if node.is_leaf: p = self._leaf_panel(node.expr)` with no try/except, while every in-round failure is funnelled into `errors[i]`. Before WP4 that was harmless: the only leaf that survives the `shape.degenerate` root check was a `Constant`, and `np.full` cannot raise. WP4 makes `DailyFeature` degenerate too, so `_leaf_panel` now calls `view.daily(field)`, which raises whenever the field is in `Registry.daily_fields` (so it parses) but not in `view.daily_fields` (so it cannot be resolved) -- exactly the `--daily-root`-not-passed misconfiguration.

Reproduced on the conftest `store` (no daily source attached):
  eng.evaluate([parse("cs_rank(FloatCap)"), parse("cs_rank(day_mean(Close))")], tolerant=True)
    -> errors == {0: "cs_rank: ValueError: dailyfields.resolve: 'FloatCap' needs a daily store carrying it (daily_root)"}, root 1 fine  (correct)
  eng.evaluate([DailyFeature("FloatCap"), parse("cs_rank(day_mean(Close))")], tolerant=True)
    -> raises ValueError out of evaluate(); the healthy second root's panel is lost too  (wrong)

`tolerant=True` is the mode every batch caller uses: gp.py:394, mining/env.py:152 (RL rewarder), mining/boosting.py:168, research.py:119, calculate.py:142, legacy/seed_library.py:35. `is_valid_root` admits a bare `DailyFeature` (expression.py:435), so a seed list, a `calculate.py` factor file or a `research.py --expr FloatCap` is enough -- and WP8 is the package that wires `--daily-root` into exactly those entry points, so it will land on this.

defects.title: _mask_cube's Constant carve-out silently skips the tradability mask for a daily-leaf chunk whose two leading dims are both 1
defects.failure_scenario:
`_mask_cube` short-circuits on `t.shape[0] == 1 and t.shape[1] == 1` (engine.py:231). That guard was written for the `Constant` reader's `torch.full((1, 1, 1), value)`. A daily-leaf chunk is `(hi-lo, D, 1)` in MODE_S and `(S, hi-lo, 1)` in MODE_D, so BOTH leading dims are 1 whenever the chunk is one row and the other axis has length 1 -- and the mask is skipped. A minute `Feature` can never reach that shape, because its last axis is M (24 in the fixture, 241 in production), so the hole arrives with WP4.

Reproduced: a one-day view (`store.view(start=dates[3], end=dates[3])`, where symbol 0 is suspended) with `chunk_symbols=1`:
  CubeEngine(v, chunk_symbols=1)._load_leaf_cube(DailyFeature("LimitWidth"), MODE_S, 0, 1, eng._tradable[0:1, :])
    -> shape (1, 1, 1), value 0.1   (a FINITE value on a stock-day view.tradable() says is suspended)
  the same cell under default chunking -> nan
So the reader itself is not chunk-invariant. The symmetric case is a one-symbol view with `chunk_days=1` in MODE_D, which I also reproduced directly (daily leaf finite on untradable day 3, minute leaf correctly NaN).

I could NOT propagate this to a wrong final panel, and I think it is inert today: the only consumers that spread a leaked cell to other cells are D-axis ops (need D > 1, impossible when MODE_S has shape[1] == D == 1) and S-axis/NT ops (need S > 1, impossible when MODE_D has shape[0] == S == 1); every elementwise / M-axis consumer keeps the leak inside its own stock-day, which the root / panel_out / boundary mask then NaNs. Reported because the reader's contract is broken, the committed shape test cannot see it (it runs with `apply_mask=False`), and the next person to add a width-1 leaf reader or relax `mask_out` inherits a live bug.
defects.suggested_fix:
Don't route the daily leaf through `_mask_cube`'s shape-sniffing carve-out -- the branch already knows the exact shape, because it asserted it two lines earlier. Replace `return self._mask_cube(t, tradable)` at engine.py:246 with:

            if self._mask_needed:
                t = torch.where(tradable.unsqueeze(-1), t,
                                torch.full((), float("nan"), dtype=t.dtype, device=t.device))
            return t

Pin it with a one-day-view / `chunk_symbols=1` test asserting NaN on a suspended stock-day (and the MODE_D mirror).

defects.title: _load_leaf_cube's daily branch hands out a tensor that writes through to view.daily()'s per-view cache
defects.failure_scenario:
In MODE_S, `view.daily_s(field, lo, hi)` returns `self.daily(name)[lo:hi, :]` (store.py:585), which is a C-contiguous VIEW of the array cached in `view._daily[field]`. So `np.ascontiguousarray(sl)` is a no-op, `torch.from_numpy(...)` shares that memory, `.to("cpu", float32)` is a no-op on the default dtype, and when `self._mask_needed` is False `_mask_cube` returns `t` unchanged. The engine then hands kernels a writable tensor aliasing the view's long-lived cache.

Reproduced:
  eng = CubeEngine(view, apply_mask=False)
  t = eng._load_leaf_cube(DailyFeature("FloatCap"), MODE_S, 0, 3, eng._tradable[0:3, :])
  t[0, 0, 0] = -1.0
  view.daily("FloatCap")[0, 0]   # 1000000000.0 -> -1.0
The corruption is not scoped to the chunk or to the call: it persists for the life of the view, across every later expression and every later evaluate().

This is the one reader without the guard the other two have. `_leaf_panel` deliberately uses `astype(..., copy=True)` for exactly this reason (and documents it), and the pre-existing `Feature` path cannot do it because `view.read_s` returns a fresh array on every call (measured: distinct objects, distinct data pointers). Today the only thing standing between this and a silently poisoned view cache is `tests/test_engine.py::test_kernels_never_write_into_operands`. Reachable whenever `_mask_needed` is False: `apply_mask=False`, or any view with no suspended/unlisted stock-days.
defects.suggested_fix: Copy in that branch, matching `_leaf_panel`: replace `np.ascontiguousarray(sl)` at engine.py:245 with `np.array(sl, dtype=self.np_dtype, copy=True)` (or `np.ascontiguousarray(sl).copy()`), and say in the comment that the copy is what detaches the engine from `view._daily`. Cost is one extra copy only on the MODE_S path -- MODE_D's slice is non-contiguous so `ascontiguousarray` already copies, and the masked path already pays it via `torch.where`. Pin it with the three-line write-through test above.

- Steps 1-9 are all present with the signatures the design names. SearchHooks fields/defaults, load_plugins (import -> register() if callable -> unconditional `catalog._DEFAULT = None` iff anything loaded -> returns names), declare_real_valued (`.update`, in place), search_hooks_from (last wins, None otherwise). Both required docstring caveats ("AlphaCube never imports a plugin on its own", "a caller holding an already-returned Registry still sees the short vocabulary") are there.
- DEFAULT-PATH IDENTITY, the strongest check I could build: I ran a default-argument GPMiner (seed 5, pop 10, max_depth 3, 3 generations) against the SAME on-disk synthetic store from the read-only baseline tree (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube, 517fd09) and from this worktree, dumping registry size, the 214 spec names, every generation's bred population keys, the archive, and the report. 308-line digests are byte-identical (script: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP7/xtree_run.py). So the whole WP1-WP7 stack, WP7's five new generator keywords included, leaves the random stream and the results untouched at the defaults, and report.generations == n_gen when nothing stops early.
- `hooks=None` vs `hooks=SearchHooks()`: SearchHooks.leaf_slots defaults to `{}` where TypedTreeGenerator defaults to `None`, so plugins.py:45's claim "Every field's default is exactly the value TypedTreeGenerator itself defaults to" is not literally true — but generator.py:574 is the only reader and it tests `if self.leaf_slots else None`, so `{}` and `None` are behaviourally identical. Harmless; the dataclass matches the design's own spec. Side effect of the dict field: `hash(SearchHooks())` raises TypeError although frozen=True suggests hashability (`==` works, which is what the tests use).
- Wall clock: `ws` falsy at the default short-circuits before time.perf_counter(); I confirmed the dedicated test is real by mutating the check to evaluate its second operand unconditionally (goes red). mine(wall_seconds=None) defers to the constructor, mine(wall_seconds=0) disables a constructor value, budget < population_size still reports 1 generation, done_gen cannot stay 0 (the loop has no early continue/break before `done_gen = g + 1`).
- DF ban keys: one_layer_keys really emits `O:cs_rank(DF:FloatCap)` (verified by parsing), the new branch sits before `F:` and cannot shadow it, `O:nt_ts_argmax(DF:FloatCap)|w3` and mixed `O:div(DF:FloatCap,F:Amt)` pass, `DF:floatcap` is rejected. End to end: banning the most frequent real daily key (`O:pow_3(DF:FloatCap)`, 10 occurrences in 400 unbanned trees) drops it to 0 occurrences.
- Exemplar cache: with no daily root attached fingerprint() is None and the hashed string is byte-identical (hand-written-hash test goes red if the append is made unconditional); with a root attached the key is stable across store reopens, so a second run hits the cache (hits=3/3).
- fitness_kind/make_scorer: scorer_kinds() is a superset of FITNESS_KINDS, built-in kinds reach PanelScorer/LongScorer with exactly today's arguments (make_scorer does not forward dates/warmup to them), a registered kind receives dates=list(view.dates) and the warmup given, and the ValueError text names the full list.
- No import cycle: `alphacube.plugins` imports cleanly first, and `alphacube.mining.gp` first works too. `default_registry()` is the only registry cache and it is lazy, so `_DEFAULT = None` is sufficient.

SMALLER OBSERVATIONS I did not file as defects
- mine()'s t0 is taken before `_add_exemplars(self._pending_exemplars)`, which the design measures at 1-2 hours for a large ban archive. A --wall-seconds smaller than the install time therefore stops the run after exactly one generation. That is what the design asked for (reuse t0), but WP8's CLI help should say the clock covers the exemplar install.
- gp.py:53 still defines its own `FITNESS_KINDS = ("ic","rank_ic","long","long_hit")`, now unreferenced in that file. Nothing imports it today, but it is a trap for WP8: a stale duplicate that will silently drift from scoring.FITNESS_KINDS. Deleting it (or re-exporting scoring's) is a one-liner.
- search_hooks_from calls `search_hooks()` on EVERY module that exposes one and keeps the last result (side effects of the discarded ones still run), does not type-check the result (a plugin returning a dict surfaces later as `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'op_weight'` inside GPMiner.__init__), and a later module whose search_hooks() returns None wipes an earlier module's hooks. All defensible readings of "last module wins".
- A failed import mid-list (`load_plugins(["good","typo"])`) raises after the good module's register() already ran and before the `_DEFAULT` reset, leaving the cached registry stale and the new kernel invisible to default_registry(). Hard-error path; the CLI dies anyway.
- SearchHooks(daily_fields=...) is never validated against registry.daily_fields. Measured: a typo'd name generates `cross_mean(FlaotCap, 60)` and every such candidate scores -inf instead of raising, so `daily_leaf_prob=1.0` plus one typo yields a run that finds nothing and says nothing. The draw site is WP5's generator, but SearchHooks is the natural place to catch it.
- `getattr(view.store, "daily", None)` tolerates a store without `.daily` but needs the view to have `.store`; a duck-typed view (no in-repo caller does this) would now raise AttributeError in GPMiner.__init__. This is verbatim what the design prescribed.

No existing "WP10:" commit was found (git log -40 checked first), so this was implemented fresh, touching only the two owned files (tokens.py + the new test file) -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` before committing.

New public names/signatures added to src/alphacube/mining/tokens.py:
- `DailyFeatureToken` (frozen dataclass, field `field: str`), placed next to `FeatureToken`, added to the `Token` Union, and to `__all__`.
- `Vocabulary.__init__` gains a new LAST keyword parameter `daily_fields: Sequence[str] = ()`, stored as `self.daily_fields` (a list), parallel to `self.fields` the way `Registry.daily_fields` is parallel to `Registry.fields`. `DailyFeatureToken(f)` tokens are appended strictly after the existing BEG/SEP/Feature/Operator/Constant/Window groups. With the default empty tuple, token order/indices are unchanged -- verified two ways: (a) a hand-written literal expected ordering with small explicit fields/constants/windows, and (b) a before/after diff over the full default registry showing every pre-existing token's index is identical and the two new tokens land at exactly `base.size` and `base.size + 1`.
- `ExpressionBuilder.push()` gains a `DailyFeatureToken` branch mirroring `FeatureToken`'s (same "unknown field" guard pattern, checked against `vocabulary.daily_fields`), pushing `DailyFeature(token.field)`. No operand-type check is added here, per the design: `DailyFeature`'s COLLAPSED/degenerate shape already flows through the existing static shape system in `_apply`/`operand_ok`.
- `ExpressionBuilder.valid_next_tokens()` now also offers `DailyFeatureToken(f) for f in v.daily_fields` as operand actions, unconditionally available like `FeatureToken` (empty list when `daily_fields` is empty, so no behavior change by default).
- New module-level helper `operator_logit_bias(vocab: Vocabulary, op_weight: Optional[Callable[[OpSpec], float]], tiny: float = 1e-9) -> np.ndarray`: a `float64` array of length `vocab.size`, `log(max(op_weight(spec), tiny))` at each `OperatorToken` index (including a negative weight, which floors the same as 0), `0.0` everywhere else (BEG/SEP/Feature/DailyFeature/Constant/Window). `op_weight=None` (matching `TypedTreeGenerator`'s own default) returns an all-zero array.

Judgment call worth flagging: the design's step 5 says "One shared op_weight then steers both searches." `TypedTreeGenerator.op_weight` accepts either a callable `spec -> float` OR a raw `{name: weight}` mapping (resolved internally by `generator._resolve_op_weight`). I made `operator_logit_bias` accept only the resolved callable form, not a raw mapping, to avoid giving tokens.py a new dependency on generator.py (today generator.py does not import tokens.py, and tokens.py importing it back, while not literally circular, would invert the apparent layering where env.py sits above both as a peer-level consumer). A caller holding a `{name: weight}` dict can still share the exact same values with both sides by wrapping it once (`lambda s: table.get(s.name, 1.0)`) -- one line, same logic `_resolve_op_weight` already does -- before passing that callable to both `TypedTreeGenerator(op_weight=...)` and `operator_logit_bias(vocab, ...)`. If a reviewer wants literal mapping support on this helper too, it's a small additive change, but I left it out since the design's explicit written steps never mention tokens.py importing from generator.py.

Confirmed, not touched: `alphasage.py`'s `_unroll()` still special-cases `DailyFeature` by looking up `FeatureToken(expr.field)` (not the new `DailyFeatureToken`) -- that file is outside WP10's owned list, so I left its "pre-WP10" comment and behavior exactly as-is. `tests/test_daily_leaf_engine.py::test_alphasage_unroll_raises_vocab_keyerror_not_attributeerror` (which pins that `_unroll(DailyFeature(...), vocab, ...)` raises `KeyError` naming the field on a vocabulary that doesn't carry a matching `FeatureToken`) still passes unchanged -- a vocabulary built with `daily_fields=(...)` now carries the field under `DailyFeatureToken`, not `FeatureToken`, so that KeyError still fires even then. Wiring `alphasage.py` (or any RL miner / pipeline.py's RL branch) to actually pass `daily_fields=` into `Vocabulary(...)` or to add `operator_logit_bias`'s output to a real policy's logits is not part of this package and I did not do it -- WP10 as scoped only adds the mechanism in tokens.py.

The suite is green on this because tests/test_daily_leaf_engine.py:462 test_alphasage_unroll_resolves_once_a_vocabulary_carries_the_token builds Vocabulary(registry, fields=list(registry.fields) + ['FloatCap']) -- a vocabulary shape WP10 does not and cannot produce -- so the one test written to cover "however WP10 arranges for that" now asserts nothing about the real path.

defects.title: operator_logit_bias turns a non-finite op_weight into a NaN/inf bias instead of rejecting it
defects.failure_scenario: math.log(max(w, tiny)) only floors the LOW end. In Python max(float('nan'), 1e-9) is nan (max returns the first argument unless the second compares greater), so a weight of NaN writes nan into the bias array, and +inf writes inf; measured in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP10/attack1.py (bias=nan, any_nan=True). Added to a policy's logits, one NaN poisons the whole row: torch.distributions.Categorical(logits=...) raises ValueError('Expected parameter logits ... to satisfy the constraint Real()') at the first sampling step, naming no operator and no field. A data-driven op_weight is the expected caller (Partura's steer arm derives weights from research output), and a mean over an empty group yields NaN. The same callable on the GP side behaves differently rather than failing: generator._pick_weighted does max(0.0, float(op_weight(s))) then `if w > 0.0`, so NaN silently becomes 0.0 and the operator is simply dropped (verified: max(0.0, nan) == 0.0). So the design's "one shared op_weight then steers both searches" (WP10 step 5) gives one arm a silent drop and the other an opaque crash, and generator._check_weight's own docstring says this guard exists so that "a NaN from some upstream computation" fails with the cause named -- WP10 re-consumes weights without it.
defects.suggested_fix: After w = float(op_weight(spec)), validate the same bound _check_weight validates: `if not math.isfinite(w) or w < 0.0: raise ValueError(f"op_weight for {spec.name!r} must be a finite float >= 0, got {w!r}")` (dropping the negative case is also defensible since the existing test pins -5.0 flooring to log(tiny), but non-finite must not pass through). Add a test asserting a NaN-returning op_weight raises with the operator name in the message.

defects.title: A duplicate name in daily_fields makes vocab.size smaller than the largest live token index
defects.failure_scenario: daily_fields is stored raw (list(daily_fields)) and the tokens are appended one per entry, so a repeated name collapses in token_to_index (last index wins) and leaves a hole: Vocabulary(reg, daily_fields=('FloatCap','FloatCap')) gives size 244 while max(index_to_token) is 244 and index 243 is missing (measured, attack1.py). Because the daily group sits at the TAIL, the live index exceeds size and TokenEnv(vocab).reset() raises `IndexError: index 244 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 244` inside action_mask (env.py:76) before a single step runs; operator_logit_bias likewise returns an array one slot too short to index. The pre-existing duplicate hazard on `fields` produces the same hole but is latent, because those indices are not at the tail (verified: Vocabulary(reg, fields=['Close','Close','Ret']) builds a hole at index 2 and TokenEnv.reset() still works), so the new parameter converts a dormant hazard into an immediate crash. Reachable from a caller, not from a default: SearchHooks.daily_fields (plugins.py:53) is a caller-assembled tuple that nothing validates on any path, so a plugin concatenating two field lists hits it.
defects.suggested_fix: Dedupe order-preservingly in __init__: `self.daily_fields = list(dict.fromkeys(daily_fields))`, or raise ValueError naming the repeated name. Same one-liner is worth applying to self.fields and self.constants. Add a test asserting Vocabulary(reg, daily_fields=('FloatCap','FloatCap')).size == base.size + 1 and that TokenEnv over it resets cleanly.
